HTML fragment colorizing the SAME real tools/list JSON-RPC reply already captured verbatim in mcp.txt (production MCP endpoint, https://beta.superbot.gg/mcp; captured on the legacy alias xdxdxd.dsh.sh) — re-flowed to <=20 lines (the description string's manual line-wrapping undone, two closing-brace pairs joined) with no value changed, then run through scripts/ansi-to-html.mjs --json, which tokenizes JSON with a regex (not a parser) and colours keys a-6 bold, string values a-2, numbers a-4, literals a-5, punctuation a-8. GAP vs. the assignment: `superbot mcp list` and `superbot status` WERE captured live against a running `SUPERBOT_HOME=~/.superbot-dev` helper (helper start/stop bracketed the capture, both succeeded) — but the live `mcp list` output enumerates this dev machine's real, personal MCP client roster (~46 servers, several named after real people/projects, e.g. a personal email-suffixed entry), which is private and not the production superbot MCP endpoint anyway. Publishing it would leak that machine's personal config for no gain over the real production JSON already on file, so it was discarded in favour of the documented mcp.txt fallback per the assignment's own fallback clause.

The 16-hex terminal palette scripts/ansi-to-html.mjs's classes (a-0..a-15) resolve against, plus the a-b/a-d/a-i/a-u weight/style classes. This is DATA for the terminal captures in this directory, not a site design-token file — the site's own token stylesheet is untouched. Indices 5/6/8/15 are pulled directly from superbot-helper's own src/cli/ui.ts swatches (MAGENTA, TEAL, MUTED, WHITE) so the rendered banner matches the CLI's real palette; the rest are conventional xterm defaults.
